outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, paying the $3,100–$15,000 fee (depending on construction cost) and submitting the preliminary plans, acoustic report, neighborhood outreach log and project narrative. What to say: The project narrative should frame the concept as continuing a bar-and-entertainment tradition on this block (cite the 2006 POE approval at 270 Columbus, the 2018 LLP at 253 Columbus, and bar operations at 256 Columbus and 527 Broadway), demonstrate how the concept supports the Broadway NCD's nightlife character, commit to the sound-mitigation measures and good-neighbor policy, and confirm that hours will close by 2 a.m. without an Extended Hours permit. Planning will route the application to environmental review, schedule the Section 311 neighborhood notification, and calendar the Commission hearing (typically 4–6 months after filing).

outcomes.original: Filing step: While the CUA is pending, engage a liquor license broker to identify and escrow an ABC Type 48 license for transfer to 270 Columbus Ave; submit the ABC transfer application only after the CUA is approved. What to say: Because San Francisco County is over quota for Type 48 licenses, the license must be purchased from an existing holder and transferred. License brokers quote Type 48 prices at $100k–$450k in San Francisco (as of 2022); expect a 90–180 day transfer timeline once ABC receives the application. Make the purchase contract contingent on CUA and ABC approval. Do not file the ABC application until the CUA is granted, because ABC will ask Planning for a zoning referral and Planning will not approve the referral until the CUA motion is final (30 days after the Commission vote).

The plan reviewer will confirm that the existing kitchen equipment, hood, grease interceptor and hand sinks meet health code requirements for the proposed use, or require upgrades. Obtain DPH plan approval before pulling the building permit, and coordinate a pre-final DPH inspection at 80% construction completion.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Once DBI issues the building permit and construction is substantially complete, schedule final inspections with DBI, DPH and the Fire Department; obtain the Certificate of Final Completion, the health permit to operate and the Fire Department Place of Assembly permit before opening. What to say: The building permit final inspection confirms that the space matches the approved plans and meets code (ADA access, exits, restrooms, mechanical systems). The DPH pre-opening inspection (schedule two weeks in advance with your plan reviewer) checks that the kitchen is operational, a certified food safety manager is on staff, and the space meets the health code; DPH issues the permit to operate after this inspection passes. The Fire Department inspects occupant load signage and the hood suppression system and issues the Place of Assembly permit. All three permits must be posted on site before the public enters. Then await ABC's final premises inspection and the Entertainment Commission's POE hearing decision.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 255 to 720 days. Estimated government cost: $23,903 to $469,400. Notes: These figures are the time and government cost to obtain the four approvals in the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, Health permit to operate, and Building permit with change of use) when they are granted. The timeline runs from forming the entity to receiving all four approvals: 8.5–24 months. The cost range includes government fees only (CUA $3,100–$15,000; POE permit $2,708; health plan check $828–$2,207 and permit $470; building permit $800–$15,000; plus business registration $55–$700, state entity formation $70–$150, sellers permit $0, EDD registration $0, food safety manager $100–$250, RBS training $50–$360 for 12 staff, fire Place of Assembly $446, FOG program $0–$500, sign permit $300–$1,500, and music licenses $600–$5,000 per year); it does not include the cost of purchasing the ABC Type 48 license ($17,000 minimum for a newly released quota license, $100,000–$450,000 for a transferred license on the open market in San Francisco as of 2022), nor the 120–300 day ABC transfer timeline, nor any professional fees (architect, acoustical consultant, license broker, attorney). The timeline assumes the CUA is approved on first hearing (4–6 months after filing) and the POE permit is approved at the first Entertainment Commission hearing (3–4 months after CUA approval); the building permit and health permits follow construction and final inspections (2–6 months). A CUA denial, a continued hearing, or a discretionary review request would extend the timeline by 3–12 months. The timeline does not account for withdrawal, denial or cancellation; the decision times block shows that two of five dated NCD-BROADWAY bar/restaurant use decisions were withdrawn (no time to approval for those cases).
